#3541. Fire Temple dungeon walkthrough in Ocarina of Time

The Fire Temple is located inside the Death Mountain Crater in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, and it's the second dungeon you'll likely encounter as an older Link.

As it's the Fire Temple, you'll need to get a Goron Tunic from Goron City to resist the heat before you go inside. However, once you're inside, you'll wish you weren't, as this hot dungeon is full of fire traps and flaming enemies. Luckily, you'll get a heavy-hitting reward if you make it through.

Before you start, we also recommend unlocking the Scarecrow Song by playing a song for the scarecrows at Lake Hylia as young Link, and then replaying the song for them after you time travel.

Here's how to complete the Fire Temple dungeon in Ocarina of Time remake.

Head up the stairs and enter the door on the left. You'll reunite with Darunia, who will tell you that Ganondorf resurrected Volvagia, an evil dragon. He'll ask you to rescue the nine Gorons trapped inside the Fire Temple before entering the boss room.

After the cutscene, jump across the platforms to your left and step on the button to free the first Goron. Then, open the chest to get a small key. The Goron will tell you about the rock hanging from the ceiling, but you can't reach it at the moment. Instead, head back to the main room.

Open the room across from you with your small key. To your left and right, you'll spot a bunch of platforms floating on top of lava. For now, jump across the platforms on your left, but be careful as the square platforms will start to sink when you touch them. Quickly make your way to the doorway and step on the button inside to free the second Goron. Open the chest inside to get a small key.

Now, make your way across the platforms to the opposite side of the room. We recommend running over to the rock wall as fast as you can, and then dealing with the Fire Keese flying around. Once they've been dealt with, blow up the rock wall with a bomb. Free the Goron inside, and open the chest to get another small key.

Return to the center of the room, and look to the north side of the room. You'll see a cube on top of a high platform. Jump across the floating platforms and wait on the square platform. This platform will actually launch up into the air rather than sink. Walk onto the platform just below the cube, and play the Song of Time. This will teleport the cube down to you. Climb the cube and head through the door.

In this room, you'll need to deal with Flying Tiles, which are literally tile monsters, and a Like Like, which looks like a giant worm. Block or hit the tiles like normal. For the Like Like, you need to avoid its attack and then go in for a hit. After you deal with them, grab the Gold Skulltula on the eastern wall.

Return to the previous room, and open the door on the east wall. There will be a fire pillar that shoots out of the ground, but there's nothing you can do in this room for now. Unlock the door ahead, and climb up either wall. Be careful of the Keese on the walls, though! Make your way to the north side of the room, and push the stone cube off the ledge. Then, drop onto the stone cube, and the fire pillar will launch you to the next floor.

In this room, you'll encounter Torch Slugs, which are slugs that attack when their back is on fire. Avoid the slugs, and quickly climb up the steps to find a blue, diamond-shaped object. Look to the right of the object to see a cube. Pull it out of the wall and place it below the fire. Then, hit the diamond-shaped object, which will swap its light to pink and turn off the fire. Climb to the top of the steps, and then shoot the diamond-shaped object with your Fairy Bow.

Climb up the wall to the third floor. This room is full of hot orbs that roll on a predetermined path. If you look at the floor near the orbs, you'll see where they'll roll. As you're walking around the room, wait for the orbs to pass you first, and then walk on by. There are four different paths you can take in this room:

First, take the quick left to get the dungeon map. Then, take the short path to the right, and blow up the rock wall to find a Gold Skulltula. Continue along the right path and step on the stone button to free the Goron. Open the chest to get a small key.

From the Goron, turn around and take the path to the right to find a locked door. Open it using the small key to enter the small room at the center of the area. Shoot the eye above the door on your right, and then head through the door. Turn right to find a chest with the compass.

Go back to the previous room, and go through the door on your right.

You'll enter a room with a bunch of metal platforms floating above lava. As soon as you jump on the metal platform, a wall of fire will appear behind you, so you'll need to quickly run to the end of the room. There is a platform with a locked door about halfway through the room, but you don't have any small keys at the moment. Additionally, a few Red Bubbles will spawn, but you can just run by them.

Push the red cube at the end of the room, and you'll end up back in the eastern half of the room. Remember the southern corner that had nothing there? Well, on the higher level, there's a captive Goron. Hop your way over, free them, and collect the small key.

Make your way to the center of the room, where you'll find a big rock pile. Blow it up with a bomb, and drop into the resulting hole. Free the Goron inside and collect the small key in the chest.

Climb back up, and head back to the platform next to the cube you pushed onto the ground. Stand near the cube, and play the Scarecrow Song. If you don't have the Scarecrow Song unlocked, you'll need to make one by the scarecrows at Lake Hylia as young Link. Then, you'll need to replay the song for the scarecrows after you've traveled into the future.

Hookshot to the scarecrow above, and then Hookshot to the platform, which will take you to the fourth floor. Go through the door, and climb up the netting. At the top, you'll find a door and a Gold Skulltula.

Go through the door, and walk toward the edge in front of you. Look to the right, and you'll see another Gold Skulltula on the wall. Use your Hookshot to retrieve it.

Then, step on the button to the left. This will create targets that you can Hookshot to, but they're slowly descending back into the ground. You'll need to quickly run up the stairs, Hookshot to the first target, jump over to the next platform, and then Hookshot to the final target. On the final platform, you'll find three chests that contain 90 rupees total.

Return to the room with the moving wall of fire and metal platforms. Now that you have a small key, you can open the door near the center of the room. Head inside, and you'll find yourself in a room with a bunch of obstacles. There are rotating pillars spewing fire, fire mazes, fake doors, and rolling red orbs again. For now, don't trust any unlocked door.

First, head north. Walk past the rotating fire totem, and then walk toward the rightmost pillar, but don't pass it just yet. If you look at the ground, you'll notice lines between each pillar and wall. Some of these lines will turn into walls of fire, but only if you get too close. As a result, this area turns into a maze with "invisible walls." As an aid, we've marked every fire wall on the image above.

Walk to the left of the rightmost pillar, and then go into the open area on your right. Free the Goron here and collect the small key in the chest.

Go back to the starting staircase, and now head south. Make your way through the fire maze to the locked door, and open it with your small key. Continue through the next door, where you'll find yourself in another fire maze.

Go right first, and make your way to the northern corner. Pick up one of the stone cubes, and bring it back to the door you just came through.

If you look northwest, you'll see a stone button in the middle of the maze. To get there, follow the path to the left. Place the stone cube onto the button to turn off all the fire traps in this area (except for the rolling balls).

Open the locked door to the west, and head inside. In this room, you'll face off against a Flare Dancer, which is a humanoid creature that cannot take damage while it's on fire. To put out the fire, use your Hookshot on its metal chest piece. Then, chase it down and attack it with your sword. If you're having a hard time catching it, run the opposite direction to cut them off. The Flare Dancer will jump back into the fire, so you'll need to repeat the process a few times until you defeat them. Later on in the fight, they'll occasionally twirl and cover themselves in more fire, but just keep firing your Hookshot at them. They will explode before they die, so make sure to take a few steps back!

After you defeat them, a platform will drop over the fire in the middle of the room. Step onto it to go to the next floor. Go into the next room, and climb up the netting on the wall. Look over the ledge to the south, and throw a bomb flower at the diamond-shaped object. Pick up another bomb flower, throw it at the diamond-shaped object, and quickly run across the line on the floor. Climb up the netting after the wall of fire disappears.

There's a button ahead of you, but don't step on it just yet. After you step on the button, a spiral staircase will lift out of the ground, and you'll need to run across it as fast as you can. We recommend jumping over to the stairs ahead of you to save some time. At the top, you'll find a chest with the Megaton Hammer inside.

Go back down the spiral staircase, and you'll find a large circular platform. Hit it with your Megaton Hammer, and the platform will fall to the lower level. Break the decorated stone statue at the end of the hall with your hammer to reveal a door. Go inside, take care of the Fire Keese, and hit the button with your Megaton Hammer to create a staircase.

Go down the stairs and through the door at the bottom. Hammer the circular platform and drop into the hole. Break the black rocks with your hammer, and you'll find a room with another time cube. Play the Song of Time (A - L - R - A - L - R) to get rid of the cube, and drop into the resulting hole. Hit the button to free the Goron, and collect the small key.

Walk onto the circular platform ahead of you, and hit it with your hammer. Remember the huge rock hanging from the ceiling near the boss room? This will drop the rock from the ceiling. Return to the starting room, and find the decorated stone statue beside the stairs. Hit it with your hammer, and open the door behind it.

This room is full of Torch Slugs. Hit one with your Megaton Hammer, and the rest of the slugs will flip over. Quickly deal with them all, and the door to the next room will unlock.

Go through the door, and take out the Flying Tiles and Like Like. Then, hit the black rock with your hammer to reveal a Gold Skulltula. Break the stone statue and go to the next room to find another Flare Dancer. Like before, use your Hookshot to pull out the metal piece in their chest, but if they're running just a little to fast, you can now use the Megaton Hammer to knock them off their feet. Don't forget to open the chest in the middle of the room to get a red rupee after you defeat them.

Head into the room to the south, and hit the button with your hammer to free the final Goron. Then, open the chest to get the boss key. Go through the door to the south, and make your way to the boss room.

When you're ready to take on the Subterranean Lava Dragon, Volvagia, go into the boss room and jump into the arena. Throughout the fight, Volvagia will cycle through three different moves:

When Volvagia first pokes their head out, you'll want to essentially play Whack-a-Volvagia with your Megaton Hammer. Run over to them as fast as you can, and hit them. If they start breathing fire, you'll have to approach them from the side. Once you hit them with the hammer, they'll fall over, and you can slash away at their head.

After, they'll launch out of a hole and either start circling the arena or fly to the center. If they fly around the arena, try to follow them along the edge of the arena. When they fly at you, the resulting lines of fire will only cover a tiny area of the arena. At first, they'll only fly at you once, but as the fight progresses, they'll do this attack at least twice.

If they fly to the center of the arena, flaming rocks will start to fall from the ceiling. Avoid standing in any shadows, and wait for this attack to subside.

Once Volvagia submerges themselves in the lava, you'll essentially just need to wait until they pop out again. Early on in the fight, Volvagia will emerge out of the third splashing hole. However, later on in the fight, multiple holes will splash at the same time, so you'll need to do a bit of guessing. The lava will splash multiple different holes before Volvagia finally decides to come out of one of them. Try to keep a bit of distance from the holes, as Volvagia can do damage to you if you're too close. Then, repeat the process by smacking their head with a hammer, and hitting them with your sword until you defeat them.

As a reward, you'll get a Heart Container, and you can exit the Fire Temple afterward via the ring of white light.

#3540. Will Ebenezer Be The Box Office Hit Johnny Depp's Hollywood Comeback Needs?

Johnny Depp is attempting to mount a Hollywood comeback. After years of being embroiled in controversy and starring in films you probably haven't heard of (like the colonial drama "Waiting for the Barbarians"), he's back in his first major studio movie in a long time. "Ebenezer" is a new take on Charles Dickens' "A Christmas Carol," with Depp playing Scrooge. The question is, can this be the box office hit that Depp needs?

Directed by Ti West ("X," "The Inkeepers"), "Ebenezer" is expected to pull in between $17 and $24 million domestically when it hits theaters next weekend, per Box Office Theory. Against a reported $38 million production budget, that would be a solid start for the Paramount release, especially since this one should be able to hang around through the holiday season. That is, assuming audiences like what West and Depp have cooked up. If it's eviscerated by critics and audiences alike? That's another conversation.

Competition shouldn't be a big issue, at least not right away. "Godzilla Minus Zero" could make box office history for the franchise topping the charts this weekend, but it shouldn't get in the way come its second frame. "The Cat in the Hat" is unlikely to be a major, direct threat, either. Rather, the biggest competition will come when "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" arrives on November 20.

The "Ebenezer" trailer positions Depp's "Christmas Carol" re-telling as being closer to a horror movie. Now, horror has been extremely hot at the box office lately, so that makes sense. Paramount is also selling the film with the tagline, "The name you know, the story you don't," and it has a star-studded supporting cast that includes Rupert Grint ("Harry Potter"), Andrea Riseborough ("Mandy"), Daisy Ridley ("Star Wars"), Trammell Tillman ("Severence"), and Ian McKellen ("X-Men").

There are obvious risks here. As mentioned, if "Ebenezer" is met with a bad response, all of these numbers could be meaningless, as word of mouth could wreck its ability to have legs. Still, it's likely to enjoy big returns on VOD and streaming, if for no other reason than curiosity from viewers.

The other issue is Johnny Depp himself. Depp dropped out of the "Fantastic Beasts" franchise after a court case verdict tied to tabloid The Sun in 2018. That, coupled with his highly-publicized courtroom battle with his ex-wife Amber Heard over allegations of abuse, derailed his career. Even before that, though, it wasn't going as well as it once had been.

Depp proved his best days were already behind him with the big box office bomb that was "Mortdecai" in 2015. He hasn't starred in a meaningful hit since 2018. Yes, the "Pirates of the Caribbean" movies made billions of dollars, but that was a long time ago. Do audiences still care about Depp? That's the big question Paramount seeks to answer. It's betting the answer is "yes."

Beyond that, Ti West has never directed a high-profile movie of this size. He helmed the "X" films rather successfully, with "MaXXXine" sending off the trilogy on a box office high note, but we're still talking about a movie that made $22 million in total. This is a big step up for West, and in light of the Depp of it all, there's a lot of pressure. Was the director able to tune out the noise and deliver a crowd-pleaser? We'll know soon enough.

"Ebenzer" hits theaters on November 13, 2026.

#3539. Of Mics and Men: After MAGA Meltdown, the Manosphere Winds Down

Two years ago, on the night of the 2024 presidential election, Ultimate Fighting Championship CEO Dana White took to the podium at Donald Trump’s Palm Beach victory party and rattled off a list of thank-yous to some rowdy podcasters and YouTube pranksters: the NELK Boys, Adin Ross, Theo Von, Bussin’ With the Boys, and “last but not least, the mighty and powerful Joe Rogan.” Just months before, these names were seldom mentioned in the mainstream press, but now they were recognized on a national stage as having powered Trump’s return to office by hosting him on their platforms and revealing his more personable side. The victory that night seemed to go well beyond the electoral conquest; one of the defining cultural legacies of the 2024 election cycle is the imprecise but vivid concept of the manosphere.

By 2026, the novelty of Trump and Von joking about the potency of cocaine, as they did in one of the signature moments of the 2024 campaign, has worn off. The president’s approval rankings tanked despite his enduring presence as a pop culture figure. Rogan endorsed Trump in the final days of that 2024 race, but he recently described Trump’s “really crazy” 1,300-word Truth Social tirade against Bill Maher as having the ring of a “girl who got dumped.” He has roundly criticized Trump’s handling of the Epstein Files, a signature issue for the podcast class, and described the Iran war as a “betrayal.” If the end of MAGA is in sight amid Tuesday’s blue tsunami, so is the notion that Republicans had captured the coveted, low-propensity demographic of young men: The New York Times estimated that Democrats won 18-to-29-year-old men by 24 points on Tuesday, a 38-point swing from Trump’s 2024 victory among them. Democrats are content creators too now, and the most notable political appearance on The Joe Rogan Experience over the past couple of years was James Talarico’s. “You need to run for president,” Rogan told Texas’s new senator-elect.

And so when C-SPAN made the somewhat mind-boggling announcement that the staid public-affairs network would simulcast election night coverage hosted by Patrick Bet-David, a Florida-based podcaster known for his interviews with Andrew Tate and Nick Fuentes, it was less of a capitulation to the so-called manosphere than an emblem of the modern media free-for-all. Of the online personalities loosely associated with Rogan’s milieu, Bet-David’s backstory is the most colorful. A refugee from Iran, he joined the Army upon arriving in the United States; he has said he worked for a time as a bodyguard to a high-level Los Angeles cocaine dealer. Bet-David now operates a media company called Valuetainment, formed after he made his riches with an insurance company that has been widely described as a multi-level marketing operation. After interviewing the leading looksmaxxing personality, Clavicular, last week, he was now responsible for providing C-SPAN’s conservative perspective. A spokesperson for the network described the programming to me as an effort to achieve “a marriage of traditional media and new media.”

“In the 2024 election, we invited Pete Buttigieg, God knows how many times, never showed up,” Bet-David told me in the lead-up to the evening. “Pete Buttigieg was here last week. We did a two-hour podcast together right before the midterms. And so the market is realizing that’s the direction you got to go.”

As he entertained a characteristically ragtag group of political-for-the-night personalities, Bet-David sat at his decision desk in a pinstripe suit with cartoonishly wide peak lapels. There were the young conservative provocateurs CJ Pearson and Nick Shirley, and the Groyper-adjacent, recent Florida gubernatorial candidate James Fishback, who described the night as a “really tough election for my party.”

Bet-David joked to Michael Franzese that he knows about gas prices—before refashioning himself as a political commentator, the former Colombo crime family capo ran a multi-million-dollar gasoline tax bootlegging scheme in the 1980s. In voicing his opposition to the war in Iran, Franzese said, “We had a saying on the street, the best way to defeat your enemies is to make them your friends.” He bemoaned how Trump “makes everything all about him.”

Other guests included Ann Coulter, Piers Morgan, Roger Stone, Bill O’Reilly, and Cenk Uygur, whose Young Turks show was simulcasting on another C-SPAN channel. For some reason, Jackass’s Steve-O appeared toward the end of the night. He pointed out to Bet-David that Marco Rubio is “stronger for you guys” than JD Vance.

Two years ago, I watched a similar scene unfold in an airplane hangar in Fort Lauderdale. It was, as Bet-David and I agreed on Tuesday, a wild night: He was hosting an election night party at Valuetainment’s headquarters at the peak of the manosphere chatter and at the onset of what seemed to so many to be the era of MAGA cultural domination. Men in tightly tapered polyester pants hopped out of Ferraris and Teslas to watch a crowd of UFC fighters, rappers, former mobsters, and Candace Owens wax poetic about how the age of Jennifer Lopez and Beyoncé, who had appeared alongside Kamala Harris in previous weeks, was over. In this new era of masculinity, there was no time anymore for liberal Hollywood political pieties: Mark Zuckerberg had just started wearing a gold chain and describing Trump’s fist pump after the attempted assassination as “one of the most badass things I’ve ever seen in my life.”

And the vibe shift, as it could only be called, was shocking for a period. There was a moment, for instance, in the heady aftermath of the 2024 election when Von attended an Oscars week poker night hosted by Timothée Chalamet at the Chateau Marmont. (The actor had recently appeared on his show.) Just weeks later, Von was at a UFC fight where White warmly embraced the Tate brothers. The entire category of celebrity appeared to be flattening in real time.

But to those on the inside of the podcaster-comedian boom, another swing of the pendulum already seemed to be coming. Andrew Schulz, a frequent Rogan guest, conducted one of Trump’s trademark podcast interviews in the summer of 2024. “After the Trump thing, I wasn’t like, ‘We got it now,’” he told me the following year. “After the Trump thing, I was like, ‘We just interviewed the president of the United States, what the fuck?’” He thought that the deafening manosphere discourse might indicate the presence of a cultural bubble. “I just think that we are what people are listening to now,” he said, “but that could change tomorrow.”

Alex Bruesewitz, a 29-year-old Trump adviser, was largely credited with orchestrating the candidate’s podcast tour in 2024. A social media operative who had built connections with big-name celebrities, influencers, and podcasters in the lead-up to the presidential election—he had brokered Trump’s alliance with Nicki Minaj and recently flew on Air Force One with Mike Tyson—Bruesewitz told me on Wednesday morning that he had soured on the Republican party.

“I consider myself more of a Trump voter than a Republican voter,” he said. “If the party moves in the direction of people like Ted Cruz, for example, in 2028, there's going to be a lot of people like myself…who will not participate in the Republican elections moving forward.”

In the midterms cycle, Bruesewitz said, the podcasting world “wasn’t there for us to engage.” The likes of Von and Schulz have echoed Rogan’s criticisms of the Iran war and how the Trump administration managed the release of the Epstein files.

“I don’t think that any of them were ever team Trump,” he said. “We simply just had conversations with them in 2024. The post-election reaction, saying that they’re part of this right-wing manosphere, I think that actually had an effect on how they covered us during our first two years. I think that they didn’t want to be labeled right-wing, and so they evened out a bit.”

Another reason, Bruesewitz supposed, for the end of Republican podcasting dominance and the blue tsunami: “Republican candidates were really lame and they weren’t interesting people…there was a little bit of an expectation that these candidates could go communicate with low-propensity voters with podcasting again, but I pushed back on their teams. I was like, Look, there’s zero percent chance that any of these podcasters are going to want to have on your boring candidates.”

By the end of the night on Tuesday, Bet-David and Steve-O were making plans to hang out before the stuntman left town. All of the guests on the C-SPAN–Bet-David collaboration seemed likely to keep talking about politics online, but it would be difficult to assign any of them a specific party agenda. In the airplane hangar two years prior, Bet-David had ended the night with what felt like a seismic exhortation, telling a raucous crowd, “For the rest of our lives we will share this night together.” On Tuesday, he was more practical as he signed off for the evening.

Bari Weiss’ public profile rose considerably back in October 2025 when David Ellison named her the editor-in-chief of CBS News. Since then, a number of pundits – those who’ve worked for the Eye Network and those who haven’t – have been weighing in on Weiss’ approach to the job. Although some have spoken out in support of the journalist/political commentator, others have criticized several of the decisions she’s made. Now, Weiss is opening up about her biggest goal for the company.

Just recently, Weiss took part in a public discussion held by Information, a technology-centric news outlet. It was during that conversation that she discussed various topics, including the concerns regarding 60 Minutes’ recent ratings decrease. Weiss was asked directly about her vision for CBS News after having been outspoken about wanting to act as a voice for “the 75% that aren’t served.” Weiss then spoke about navigating news in this social and political landscape before saying that her vision was built on one detail – trust:

Everyone in this room knows that we’re living in an era of collapsing trust. And so that is first and foremost the goal – build a news organization, a mass news organization that is deserving of trust. I think, a lot of times people talk about, ‘We have a crisis in trust.’ No, we have a crisis in trustworthiness. A lot of media organizations, especially in the mainstream, especially over the past decade, either ignored or misconstrued major stories that ere of incredible, national, even international significance. And so that is the reality, that is the landscape in which I’m building CBS.

How Bari Weiss Responded After Being Asked If She’d Like To Run CNN

Trust has been a significant topic of discussion regarding CBS News since Weiss began running the outlet. Amid her tenure, there have been claims of editorial partiality, with some former employees claiming they were pressured to insert what they considered to be bias into their reporting. Weiss herself has denied the allegations of “journalistic interference” and, based on the comments she shared at the recent discussion (via YouTube) she’s looking to build trustworthiness.

Alleged editorial bias isn’t the only reason some have taken issue with Weiss. Before being hired to join CBS, she founded an online media outlet, The Free Press, which was purchased by the now-defunct Paramount Skydance. Former 60 Minutes alum Scott Pelley – who was fired for allegedly accusing Weiss of “murdering” the show – has spoken about her apparent lack of experience in traditional broadcast journalism. Pelley argues that his former workplace is in need of “adult supervision.” Despite the issues with Weiss’ background, she seems keen on taking elements of both traditional and non-traditional practices:

The second thing, and we’ve done this, I think, in a really powerful way at The Free Press — obviously CBS is totally different scale — is how do you marry the energy and vibrancy and vitality of the independent creator world, for lack of a better term, and marry it to the rigor and standards of great news organizations like the ones that we work for?

While Pelley and veteran broadcaster Dan Rather have expressed disapproval of Weiss’ work, some of her current employees have come to her defense. Current CBS Evening News anchor Tony Dokoupil said he hadn’t experienced any news bias and spoke positively of Weiss’ leadership. Sir Trevor Phillips – CBS News’ newly hired senior global affairs correspondent and 60 Minutes contributor – also defended Weiss’ running of the brand. Phillips made note of his boss’ attempts to build an effective, new team moving forward.

With the media landscape continuing to evolve, it’s likely that CBS News will have to further confront changes in one way or another. Time will tell, of course, how Bari Weiss and co. choose to respond to shifts in the industry.

#3537. Andy Weir Reveals The Tricky Issue With The Project Hail Mary Audiobook [Exclusive]

"Project Hail Mary" pulled off a bit of a magic trick, mixing hard sci-fi with a family-friendly adventure to create something that's part Disney movie, part "Interstellar." That unlikely mix is encapsulated in Rocky, the crab-like alien from the planet Erid with whom Ryan Gosling's space traveler Ryland Grace forms an unbreakable bond. Rocky was puppeted and voiced by James Ortiz, alongside several other puppeteers, and he's not only a lovable supporting character who wouldn't be out of place in a Pixar film, he's a representation of Andy Weir's hard sci-fi leanings to boot.

The author, who wrote the 2021 novel on which "Project Hail Mary" is based, chose not to use a humanoid form for the alien, in defiance of years of Hollywood tradition. He also chose to have Rocky communicate in a uniquely alien way. Indeed, the Eridian uses musical tones and chords to speak, prompting Grace to create a makeshift translation system that allows him to converse with Rocky. In the audiobook, however, Rocky's unusual form of communication presented a challenge.

Weir has spoken positively about the "Project Hail Mary" audiobook, which is narrated by the great Ray Porter. Porter speaks as Rocky as well, but he's accompanied by musical tones to represent the actual sound of the alien's communication. A lot of thought went into defining Rocky's voice for the audiobook this way, too, as /Film's Jeremy Mathai when he interviewed Weir about this choice.

In "Project Hail Mary," James Ortiz provided the perfect voice for Rocky, not only striking an endearing, friendly tone for an alien unfamiliar with human customs but also the feel of the computerized translation system. In fact, the Rocky actor previously pointed out a subtle detail most will have missed in "Project Hail Mary," whereby he introduced glitchy computer sounds into his actual on-set performance.

For the audiobook, however, Ray Porter was in charge of reading Rocky's dialogue, and while he was more than capable of the task, Andy Weir and the team behind the audiobook's creation wanted to convey the alien's musical form of communication at the same time. In his interview with /Film, Weir recalled how there were "a lot of discussions on how to do special effects" for the "Project Hail Mary" audiobook. "How do we do Rocky in the book, because the movie hadn't come out yet?" he continued. "So, it was just, how do we present these musical notes? Well, we can play musical notes."

The "Project Hail Mary" audiobook begins with Porter reading Rocky's translated dialogue accompanied by these musical notes to represent how the alien's language sounds pre-translation. But as the story goes on, Ryland Grace gets to the point where he's able to understand his alien pal without needing a translation. As Weir explained:

"It's like, 'Okay, but later on, Grace is just understanding what Rocky's saying,' and so they did this transition of the musical notes are loud toward the beginning of the book, and then by the end of it, you can barely hear the musical notes at all. That's supposed to be representative of Grace learning the Eridian language more and more."

"Project Hail Mary" is full of hidden details, and it seems the same is true of the audiobook, which is surely one of the best examples of the form in recent years. Ray Porter is an excellent Ryland Grace, winning the 2022 Audie Award for Science Fiction and Audiobook of the Year for his performance. But Andy Weir and the producers also clearly thought very hard about how best to convey Rocky's unique form of communication, revealing a deep attention to detail. As Weir put it, "I thought they did a great job, but we went back and forth, had a lot of conversations about how to make that happen."

The pairing of musical notes with Porter's narration is, itself, a great representation of how the audiobook maintains that remarkable mix of hard sci-fi and wholesome entertainment that makes the original book and its film adaptation so effective. To be sure, while Porter keeps listeners invested with his enthusiastic, genial narration, the music maintains a sense of this being a truly alien and otherworldly experience. Making the music fade as Ryland Grace becomes more familiar with Rocky's language is just the cherry on top.

For now, Weir isn't planning a sequel to his original story. But in the meantime, there are plenty of sci-fi books you simply have to listen to if you loved Ray Porter's "Project Hail Mary" narration.

#3536. If You Loved 'Carrie,' There's One Movie You Need to Watch Next

Jeff Somers is a freelancer who has been writing about writing, books, personal finance, and home maintenance since 2012.

Jeff has published nine novels and more than 70 short stories; his story Ringing the Changes was selected for inclusion in The Best American Mystery Stories 2006. This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Stephen King’s Carrie is one of those endlessly rebootable stories. Way back in 1974, King zeroed in on a near-perfect horror setup that explored being othered, the emotional and mental health consequences of bullying, and just how crappy being a teen girl can be in the modern world. Those themes—and the iconic visuals King conjured with his words—are evergreen, and resonate with audiences each time the story gets rebooted. Mike Flanagan has proved himself a master of horror and a clear successor to King’s legacy in the genre, and if you thought his Carrie reboot on Prime Video was terrific (and you’ve watched all the similar series out there), you should really watch Jennifer’s Body.

Carrie and Jennifer’s Body share a lot of themes—the corrosive pressure of high school, the casual cruelty of adolescents, the explosive power of feminine anger. While Jennifer Check (Megan Fox) is superficially presented as having more power and control than Carrie White (Summer H. Howell) because she’s more self-possessed (and played by Megan Fox), underneath the hair and makeup, Jennifer is just as naive and confused as Carrie. Both girls endure horrific experiences that set them on a path to horrific violence—and those experiences are symbolic of what women everywhere have to deal with all the damn time.

Just as in Carrie, Jennifer’s Body tracks a teen girl’s descent into monstrousness—but where Carrie leans into the tragic nature of those themes, Jennifer’s Body offers a funnier, more sarcastic take buoyed by Diablo Cody’s sharp dialogue and laugh-out-loud moments. The series highlights Carrie’s suffocating home life that offers her no relief from the grinding hell of being a 16-year-old girl who doesn’t quite fit the expected physical or behavioral norms imposed on teen girls, tracing a slow boil of rage. Jennifer’s Body depicts a character who ultimately chooses the dark path, leaning into her newfound destructive power, and has more fun with it, making it the perfect complement to the series.

Although the stories take different paths to get there, they both wind up at a cathartic and bloody climax centered on a school dance, where a lot of people die and chaos reigns. The film is the perfect way to examine, from a different angle, the themes that Carrie explores. Stream Jennifer’s Body on Hulu or rent it on Prime Video.

Looking for more stories about angry teen girls teaching society a terrifying lesson? Here are a few more films that make a perfect pairing with Carrie.

It’s been 50 years since Brian De Palma adapted King’s novel for the first time, and it’s still worth watching today, especially if you enjoyed Flanagan’s modern take. What could have been a trashy horror movie designed to cash in on the book’s success is instead a well-crafted film that makes every character feel real and consequential, and Sissy Spacek’s performance as Carrie is screen-meltingly amazing. Few horror films have aged this well, and watching a different creator’s vision of the story will be well worth your time. Rent Carrie on Prime Video.

If Carrie’s cathartic presentation of female rage and teen angst is what hooked you, the most relevant movie to jump to is The Craft. The story of four high school girls who harness dark powers to take revenge on, well, high school life itself is anchored by four feral performances from Robin Tunney, Fairuza Balk, Neve Campbell, and Rachel True. Like Jennifer’s Body, the teen protagonists enthusiastically embrace their power in a way that Carrie White doesn’t, but it transforms (and destroys them) just the same. Rent The Craft on Prime Video.

One reason Carrie is terrifying in all its forms? The very idea of a child with an imperfect grasp of ethics and an immature emotional state having thermonuclear-level psychic powers. After all, teenage girls without powers can be terrifying when triggered. The Innocents focuses on sisters Ida (Rakel Lenora Petersen Fløttum) and Anna (Alva Brynsmo Ramstad), who meet Ben (Sam Ashraf) and Aisha (Mina Yasmin Bremseth Asheim), who both demonstrate powers including telekinesis and mind control. Their interaction soon reveals that Anna also has mental powers, and the four begin working to enhance their capabilities—but when one of them begins using their powers to hurt others and seek revenge, things take a dark turn that fans of Carrie will appreciate. Stream The Innocents on Kanopy or rent it on Prime Video.

Anyone who was ever bullied in the teen years (so ... everyone) knows that those wounds never quite heal. That’s one aspect of Carrie’s power, and it’s also what makes Sissy an ideal movie to watch when you’ve finished the series. A mental health influencer, Cecilia (Aisha Dee)—once known as “Sissy”—runs into her old best friend, Emma (Hannah Barlow) and is unexpectedly invited to Emma’s bachelorette weekend—only to run into her childhood tormentor, Alex (Emily De Margheriti). The old trauma hits Cecilia like a bomb, shattering her fragile mental balance and leading to a surprisingly funny series of murders as Sissy works through her lingering anger issues. Stream Sissy on Hoopla or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

If you’re a Mike Flanagan and Stephen King superfan, the obvious movie choice is their other collab, Doctor Sleep. A sequel to one of the most famous horror stories of all time (The Shining), the story finds a middle-aged Danny Torrance (Ewan McGregor) struggling to control his psychic powers, and leading the fight against an ancient group of entities that feed off of people like him. If you want more of that Flanagan/King magic, this is the right move. Rent Doctor Sleep on Prime Video.

Whenever I see one of Matt Damon’s daughters in an interview with him, I just wait for them to roast him about something. He shares four daughters (Alexia, Isabella, Gia, and Stella) with his wife, Luciana Barroso, and they never fail to tell their dad EXACTLY what they think about his work, his clothes, and even the way he stands. So naturally, when he took his daughter, Isabella, to the 2026 CFDA Fashion Awards, she wouldn’t be able to resist roasting her dad’s style (and I can’t get over his reaction).

The actor has often shared stories about his daughters’ opinions, so he should know what to expect by now. We already know they have no problem telling their dad the honest truth, even calling out his ‘bad’ movies. So, I knew what Isabella was going to say when an Elle reporter asked for her opinion on her dad’s style. Sure enough, she was quick to throw her dad to the fashion police by assuring she has to veto his outfit choices “every day” and credits a house full of women for giving him a helping hand. Check out the funny moment:

Now, we can’t discount her sisters when it comes to keeping Damon on his toes. Her sister, Gia, has critiqued not just Damon but his BFF Ben Affleck for their red carpet poses when the duo was promoting their movie The Rip. In this case, given the way he laughs (and instantly agrees), he knew what was coming when a reporter asked his daughter if she has vetoed any of his looks. It’s sweet to see how quickly Damon agrees with her, claiming that without her (plus, her mom and sisters) he’s “pretty hopeless.” (Though I wonder if his fashion sense is something that annoys Affleck, since we already know what annoys Damon.)

However, the most surprising part of the interview was that Odysseus received the best dressed award out of Damon’s characters. (Perhaps because it’s the most recent movie Damon has done, having hit the 2026 movie schedule over the summer?) The shout-out is ironic given the cold and wet conditions the actor often found himself in during his ‘odyssey.’ While he doesn’t disagree that his epic hero looks his best (and the costuming is fantastic), he does have a different opinion on which of his characters has the best style:

Though Tom Ripley has pretty great style. After -- once he met Dickie Greenleaf. Once Dickie came into his life, he had good style.

Tom Ripley is the titular con artist from The Talented Mr. Ripley (1999), and it is set in the 1950s. Now, I don’t knock the fun costuming in the movie, but it wasn’t the character I expected. I would have thought Jason Bourne would at least get a shout-out for his attire. After all, it is one of the few roles Damon has done multiple times. Maybe it’s the ‘50s aesthetic that won Damon’s favor.

Anyway, getting back to the actor's personal style, he did look very nice at this event...and I bet his daughters and wife had something to do with that. Now, as award season kicks into high gear, I'll be curious to hear about any fashion vetoes they throw their dad's way.

#3534. Laura Loomer, Elon Musk, George Santos, and More React to Election Night: “I Hope Everyone Is Learning Arabic”

The midterm elections marked a night of historic firsts: Adam Hamilton became the first Democratic senator elected in Kansas in nearly 100 years; Chris Pappas is now the first openly gay man to be voted into the Senate; Keisha Lance Bottoms is the first Black woman to be elected as a US governor; Bentley Hudgins is the first transgender and nonbinary lawmaker to be voted into the Georgia General Assembly—the list goes on.

How better to chronicle a generational evening in US history than on social media? Our founding fathers recounted watershed moments via post riders and printed broadsides; in the mid-19th century, dispatches were sent via the Pony Express. President Lincoln’s shooting was rushed to the public via Morse code tapped over the wires, and during World War I, we utilized undersea telegraph cables. Yet in our long history spanning radio broadcasts, satellite television, and smoke signals, nothing has quite captured the zeitgeist like an X post.

“CNN is now saying the national anthem has been changed to a reggaeton cover of Pink Pony Club,” tweeted one user last night, right as the media joined a chorus of policy analysts and pundits to announce a new dawn as Democrats took control of Congress—a blue wave. Or rather, a blue tsunami.

Social media users across the country then took to X to mourn, deny, or celebrate the victory. Yet amid the cacophony of social media’s tweets, posts, replies, comments, and reels, the most notorious influencer grew shockingly quiet: President Donald Trump himself. Despite posting a half-hearted image of a MAGA-red hat reading “VETO,” Trump has not said much online in the hours following the victory.

In the months leading up to the midterms, social media did more than simply sway victories. In fact, it propelled candidates like Jon Ossoff to the forefront through short-form vertical videos, made contenders such as Abdul El-Sayed go viral through clips set to songs like Eminem’s 2010 hit “Not Afraid,” and directed Gen Z focus to key races through memes (“TEXAS JUST WENT BLUE. PUT PRONOUNS BACK IN YOUR BIO NOW,” New York City Council member Chi Ossé posted in his Instagram Stories last night).

More than three quarters of young adults relied on social media or platforms like YouTube as a source for their midterm election news this year. An astounding 67% of millennials also got the lowdown from content creators. Call it absurd, call it brain rot, or call it sensational: There’s no doubt that social media has become a phenomenon, and the Twitterverse is still alive and well in 2026.

#3533. Jeremy Allen White As Wolverine? Marvel Reportedly Met Actor For X-Men Reboot

It looks like it may finally be time to find the next Wolverine, and an Emmy-winning actor may well be in talks to take on the role of Marvel's beloved mutant. Hugh Jackman famously replaced Dougray Scott as Wolverine in "X-Men" and, well, he never gave up the role. He's been playing the part since 2000 and most recently reprised the part in "Deadpool & Wolverine." But Marvel Studios is building out a new future for the X-Men, and if a new report is to be believed, Jeremy Allen White could be our new Logan.

According to the InSneider, the hunt for the next Wolverine is on, and there are "whispers" that the "Deliver Me From Nowhere" and "The Bear" star has met with Marvel to discuss "what is expected to be a small role in its upcoming 'X-Men' reboot." However, the role "would lead to more screen time down the line. A lot more." For now, that's all we know, but that in and of itself is pretty darn significant.

Marvel's new cast of mutants for the "X-Men" reboot was revealed at D23 back in August. That cast includes Christopher Abbott ("Kraven the Hunter") as Charles Xavier, Inde Navarrette ("Obsession") as Rogue, and Adam Driver ("Star Wars") as the villain Mr. Sinister. Notably absent from the lineup was a new Wolverine. Based on this new report, it sounds like Marvel might hold him back for most of this movie, teeing him up for a larger role down the line.

If White does indeed take on the role, he's got some big shoes to fill. To say that Jackman is beloved as Wolverine would be an understatement. But Jackman's Wolverine was one of the Major Marvel characters left out of the "Avengers: Doomsday" cast announcement. That raised some eyebrows, though that doesn't mean he won't appear in the movie.

Is it that Hugh Jackman's appearance as Wolverine is being kept a secret? Is Marvel Studios holding him back for "Avengers: Secret Wars" as a likely swan song for his version of the character? Production on "Secret Wars" has moved to 2027 and a delay may be coming, but we'll know more about that after "Doomsday" comes out. Right now, we have more questions than answers but either way, it seems like his time donning the claws may finally, truly be coming to an end.

Jeremy Allen White is an in-demand actor who has beefed up big time for roles in the past, most notably "The Iron Claw." He's got the physique, and he seems to be the right actor at the right time. While he's certainly got momentum, "The Social Reckoning" just flopped at the box office, and his Bruce Springsteen biopic wasn't quite as buzzy of a hit as it was expected to be.

In short, a splashy role like Wolverine could be just what he needs right now and he also fits the bill when it comes to what Marvel is looking for as it builds out the future. It's the right pairing at the right time.

Jake Schreier ("Thunderbolts") is set to direct the new "X-Men" movie, which is expected to go into production soon. Plot details are being kept under wraps but that probably has a lot to do with the fact that "Doomsday" and "Secret Wars" are going to completely reshape the MCU as we know it.

The "X-Men" reboot is set to hit theaters on May 5, 2028.

#3532. Ice Cavern dungeon walkthrough in Ocarina of Time

The Ice Cavern is a shorter dungeon in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, but it's a necessary one. The Zora Domain and its surrounding areas have been covered in ice, but you need to reach the end of this icy cave to retrieve the Iron Boots.

To get through the Ice Cavern, you'll need to defeat freezing enemies, collect ice crystals, push ice blocks, and defeat a furry foe all while looking out for falling stalactites.

Here's how to complete the Ice Cavern dungeon in Ocarina of Time remake.

Before you start sliding into the icy dungeon, we recommend putting on headphones or increasing your volume, as there are a lot of deadly ice stalactites that might fall on you. One of the easiest ways to avoid them is to listen for the crunchy noises that they make just before they fall.

Additionally, you'll need an empty bottle. The more you have, the better, but for the sake of this guide, we'll imagine you only have one empty bottle available.

Shuffle into the Ice Cavern, watch out for stalactites, and slash your way through the stalagmites. Toward the end of the path, you'll encounter a few Freezards. They have an icy breath that will freeze you if you get hit, so wait for them to finish breathing before you start attacking them. You can also use your Hookshot on them to quickly get into close range. For the Blade Traps, try to get the Freezards to breathe on them, which will stop them in place. After you've dealt with all the Freezards, the way ahead will be unlocked.

In the next room, you'll need to collect five ice crystals in order to proceed. Break the stalagmites on your left and collect the first crystal. Then, turn to the southern wall and look up to find a Gold Skulltula. Use your Hookshot to retrieve its token. Collect the three ice crystals in the middle of the room, but don't try to jump over the spinning fan. Instead, walk with the blades and jump when you're under the crystals. Then, climb up the stairs, wait for the ice blade to pass, and jump for the floating ice crystal. Now, you should have all five crystals, and the gate will unlock.

Head into the next room, and you'll see a bunch of frozen platforms. There is a Freezard on one of the platforms, and they're just waiting for you to climb up. Climb up to their platform, and quickly run behind the Freezard before it freezes you. Then, take it out with a few swings. There are also a few Ice Keese flying around. Either wait for them to swoop down at you or use your bow to take them out. Lastly, Freezards will spawn on the ground, so be careful if you fall, as there are quite a few down there.

Jump up to the last platform, where you'll find an ice stalagmite in front of red ice blocks. Break the stalagmite, and blue fire will melt the red ice away. Take out an empty bottle, and collect some of the blue fire. We recommend using as many empty bottles as you can. Continue along the path, and you'll find a Freezard and a chest encased in red ice. Take out the Freezard, and then use the blue fire to melt the red ice. Open the chest to get the dungeon map, and make sure to refill your bottle with blue fire before you go.

Head back to the previous room with the rotating blade. There are two chunks of red ice: one to your left and one to your right. First, head to the ice on your left, but be careful of the pots, as they're actually Flying Pots that will charge straight at you. Block them with your shield, and then melt the red ice.

Follow the path ahead, and make the Freezard freeze the Blade Trap. From here, you can either bait the Freezard to freeze the second Blade Trap, or you can defeat them and try to quickly roll past the trap. Once you get past, you'll enter a room with red ice, a chest, and another source of blue fire, but be careful of the Ice Keese hiding behind the stalagmites. Break the stalagmites in front of the blue fire, defeat the Ice Keese, and bottle some fire.

Use the fire to melt the red ice, and you'll find two pots with blue rupees and fairy thoughts scribbled onto the wall. The fairy will wish to feel the sun, so play the Sun's Song by the markings, and your health and magic will be fully restored. Don't forget to refill your bottle with blue fire!

Break the stalagmites in front of the chest, defeat the Ice Keese, and open it to find the compass. Turn around, and you'll see a Gold Skulltula on the wall. Use your Hookshot to get its token.

Return to the room with the rotating ice blade, and melt the red ice on the lower level. Follow the path through the stalagmites, but be careful of the falling stalactites. Take out the Ice Keese, and step onto the large frozen platform. Turn around and look at the wall to find a Gold Skulltula. Waddle up to the edge, and use your Hookshot to retrieve it.

In this room, you'll need to collect five ice crystals again to unlock the door. Four of the crystals are on top of the pillars in the center of the room. The last crystal is encased in red ice on the north side of the room. Collect the crystal on the lowest pillar. For the remaining crystals, you'll need to push the square ice block around the room, and use it as a stepping stone to reach the others.

To collect the rest of the crystals, push the ice block in these directions: south, west, north, and then east. Don't forget to climb onto the pillars and collect the crystals before you push the block again.

Now, push the ice block to the west, south, and west again. The ice block should end up just below the blue fire. Before you climb up, shuffle a bit to the north, and you'll see a familiar symbol on the wall. This symbol can be found at the Temple of Time and on the time cubes in the other dungeons. Play the Song of Time (A - L - R - A - L - R) and a bridge will appear. Climb up the ice block, collect some blue fire in a bottle, and cross the bridge to the chest. Open it to get a red rupee.

Drop down and just push the ice block off the edge. It'll respawn in its original position. Now, push the ice block west and then north. The ice block should be just below the red ice. Climb up, melt the ice, and collect the crystal, which should open the door to the south.

Drop down and shove the ice block off the edge again. You'll need to repeat the original four directions (south, west, north, and east), but then you'll need to finish it off with one shove to the south. This will put the ice block just below the open doorway. Climb up and head inside.

Go up the steps to the left, but be careful of the stalactites at the top. Bottle up some blue fire, and then defeat the Freezard to the south. Climb up, and there will be another Freezard waiting for you. Wait out its icy breath, and then defeat it. Use your blue fire to melt the red ice, and then head through the door.

In this room, you'll face off against a White Wolfos, which are like their regular Wolfos counterparts, but if you get hit by their attacks, you'll freeze. Backflip just before they swing so that they miss both their attacks, and they'll spin around, leaving their back open to attacks. After you defeat them, open the chest to get Iron Boots.

A cutscene with Sheik will start immediately after, and Sheik will tell you that Princess Ruto has fled to the Water Temple. Sheik will also teach you the Serenade of Water (L - R - A - A - Y), which can be used to teleport to the Water Temple's grounds in Lake Hylia.

Follow the path to the south, and bottle some blue fire, which you'll need to melt King Zora. Then, open the Equipment menu, and put on the Iron Boots. After you equip them, you can quickly take them off or put them back on by pressing Down on the D-pad. Walk into the water and you'll sink to the bottom. Walk out and you'll end up back at Zora Fountain, but don't forget to take off the boots to get back to the surface.

#3531. Google's 'Health Guardian' Is Now Available for Fitbits

Google’s “Health Guardian” feature set rolled out in late September to Pixel Watches 3, 4, and 5, and is now coming to Fitbit Air users in a new update. Google says the new features include reports on your blood pressure trends and on insulin resistance, which is a big claim for a wearable. Here’s what we know about Health Guardian, including how to set it up and what to expect.

Insulin resistance is associated with type 2 diabetes, and can be an early sign that you are heading toward pre-diabetes or diabetes. When your body’s insulin receptors stop responding as strongly to insulin, you’re more likely to have higher blood glucose.

Insulin resistance is normally measured with bloodwork. For example, your fasting glucose levels and fasting insulin are combined into a score called HOMA-IR. If you’re concerned about insulin resistance or pre-diabetes, it’s best to talk to an actual healthcare professional to find out what tests they recommend, and what to do with the results.

The insulin resistance feature coming to Google Health is, Google notes, “not intended for medical purposes” and “not a pre-screener for diabetes.”

Google published a paper describing some of the testing that went into developing its insulin resistance algorithm. In the study, the researchers had people use their own Fitbits or Pixel Watches to record a variety of metrics, including heart rate, HRV, and activity. It’s not clear from this paper exactly how the algorithm works or whether it’s likely to be useful in a general population, but apparently Google is betting on it being an interesting factor to track in your Google Health app.

Google also published a paper on a blood pressure algorithm, although it is not peer-reviewed. Instead of explaining how the algorithm works, it describes how the researchers tried to figure out what their AI-based model might be looking at. According to this paper, Google's model works about as well as clinical blood pressure measurements, but it's not clear how useful it would be in the real world. For example, the study excluded people with heart disease, but I'd imagine plenty of people with heart disease would be interested in their blood pressure scores.

Google said last month in a press release that Health Guardian, which includes insulin resistance and blood pressure trends, is available for free for people who use a Pixel Watch 3, 4, or 5. Fitbit Air users, they added, would get blood pressure and insulin resistance trends “with a Google Health Premium subscription later this year.” "Later" has arrived, as the feature for Fitbit users is in Google Health 5.11, available on both Android and iOS.

So it’s free if you have a Pixel Watch, but not if you only have the Fitbit Air: Google Health Premium is $9.99/month. It’s unclear what happens if you own both devices; presumably, having a Pixel Watch will get you free access. In any case, other devices, including older Fitbits, do not seem to be included.

The Pixel Watch got Health Guardian in the 5.09 release of the Google Health app for Android. The Fitbit got Health Guardian in the 5.11 release for both Android and iOS.

You can set up your blood pressure and insulin resistance tracking as soon as you get the new version of the Google Health app. I was able to set up insulin tracking by going to the health tab and then tapping Metabolic, and I set up blood pressure under Heart. If you go to Respiratory, you can also set up sleep-breathing quality. (Some European users will get a feature that can call for help in a "breathing emergency," but that is not available in the U.S.)

Google said that the insulin and blood pressure features will give you a monthly report on the first of each month, with the first report coming Oct. 1, if you have given the watch enough data in the previous month. If you're a Fitbit user and are just setting up the feature now, you'll get your first report on Nov. 1. Here is what the app requires:

For blood pressure reports: You need to wear the watch for five consecutive days in the previous month (so, in October to get your November report). You don't have to wear the watch at night.

For insulin resistance: You need to wear the watch for seven days and nights in the previous month, but they don't need to be consecutive.

I set up both features as soon as I got the update for the Pixel Watch, but that timeline didn't allow me a full seven days and nights before the October report. That means I don't have an insulin resistance result. I do have my blood pressure trend result: "Not High." As a reminder, a watch cannot know your actual blood pressure, so the watch is making estimates based on data that may not correspond with your actual blood pressure. That said, my blood pressure tends to read in the normal range at doctors' visits, so at least this wasn't surprising.

What's more confusing is what you're actually supposed to do about the results. If your watch says your blood pressure or insulin are fine, would you delay seeking care or abandon a treatment or lifestyle change that was supposed to help you? If your watch says something is wrong, would you believe that and maybe spend unnecessary time and money getting checked out? Pixel Watch users are discussing their results online, with a variety of reactions. One redditor says: "I awoke to find out that my blood pressure is too high and apparently the insulin in my body does nothing. This despite that my most recent doctor's visit and blood work were all perfectly normal." Another said: "I got this high insulin result this morning. I have really changed my diet the last four months and I have been going to the gym regularly. I have lost about 40 pounds this year. It's a bummer to see this. I just wonder if it's accurate." I wonder that, too.

Warning! The following contains spoilers for The Greatest. Stream the series with a Prime Video subscription, and read at your own risk!

One of the latest sports series to hit the small screen, The Greatest runs through the early years of Cassius Clay's career in boxing and his eventual transformation into the icon we all know as Muhammad Ali. The first episode highlights his time immediately after the Olympics back in Louisville, Kentucky, and how the frustrations between his treatment there and back in Rome led him to launch his gold medal into the Ohio River.

To be quite honest, that scene is one of the most shocking things I've seen on the 2026 TV schedule. I've watched a lot about Muhammad Ali in my life, and I wasn't familiar with this moment. It was wild to think one of the most famous gold medals in United States history was sitting at the bottom of a river, but it turns out the truth behind that story is widely disputed.

It didn't take long for me to discover some information on this situation. Apparently, while the story of Cassius Clay launching his gold medal into the river after being denied service at a diner because of his race is a well-known legend, it is often disputed by historians. Even though Ali famously recalled the story in his 1975 autobiography, some within his inner circle hinted that while the restaurant story happened, Clay had lost the medal in a move a year later.

American television producer Dick Ebersol later wrote in Sports Illustrated that Ali had told him that he "simply lost" the medal at some point. It made for a great dramatic moment in The Greatest, but there's more evidence than not that the event itself simply never happened.

As mentioned, The Greatest is all about the life of Cassius Clay, specifically the early years of his boxing career after his Olympic Gold Medal win in Italy. The story is largely about what happened between those big bouts as well as the issues Clay and his family experienced in their quick rise to fame.

Boxing Trainer Shares How Will Smith ‘Fell To His Knees’ After Particularly Brutal Training For Muhammed Ali

The show -- which is executive-produced by Michael B. Jordan -- also focuses on Clay's friendship with Malcolm X and how he became a major advocate for the treatment of Black Americans after witnessing equality while overseas in Italy. The premiere is a powerful one, showing how Cassius slowly witnesses just how different life is back home in Louisville, and the number of people quickly coming into his life to potentially take advantage of him as much as to help him.

As someone who loves some of the best sports movies as much as the next person, I'm really enjoying The Greatest. While there hasn't been a ton of boxing-oriented action thus far, there's plenty to learn about the fighters' lives, including that of one of Ali's most memorable opponents, Sonny Liston. Sure, some creative liberties are taken, but so far, there's more fact than fiction I'm spotting in this riveting series. You might even say it deserves a gold medal of its own.

Watch The Greatest on Prime Video right now. I've often argued that November is the best time to watch boxing shows and movies, and this series is proving me right!

#3529. My Favorite Travel Headphones Are $250 Off Right Now

As a headphone reviewer, not many headphones outside of the flagship Sony, Bose, and Apple models get me excited. However, the JBL Tour One M3 Smart Tx headphones became the exception to that rule when I started using them over my Sony 1000XM6 as my go-to headphones. And right now, the Tour One M3s are down to $199.95 (originally $449.95), their lowest price ever, according to price-tracking tools. This is a great deal for these headphones, which I deemed my favorite travel headphones in my review.

Everything from design to the features on the Tour One M3 was made with travel in mind. The headphones are very light, which, along with the comfortable soft earcups and headband, makes them great for wearing for long periods of time. I was able to wear these on a long flight without feeling any discomfort. Feeling like you're not wearing any headphones is the gold standard for comfort, and the Tour One M3 nails that aspect. The battery life is also impressive, with up to 70 hours with ANC off and 40 hours with it on.

The travel case is compact, convenient, and has extra storage for the audio transmitter, which is the best feature of the Tour One M3. This is a high-quality, low-latency audio transmitter. Anything that you can plug an AUX cable, USB, or USB-C port into can stream high-quality, 24-bit audio wirelessly to the Tour One M3. The main way most people will use these headphones is by plugging them into the in-flight entertainment, which lets you watch movies in high-quality LDAC with ANC. But I've also been able to use them to watch TV.

The Tour One M3 Smart Tx are incredible traveling headphones, especially at $199.95, and I recommend them to anyone who values comfort, battery life, simplicity, and likes the idea of the audio transmitter.

#3528. Backrooms Star Renate Reinsve Reportedly Met Marvel For Major X-Men Movie Role

Norwegian actor Renate Reinsve's star has risen, and Marvel Studios is reportedly taking notice. According to Knight's Edge Media, Reinsve recently took a meeting with Marvel Studios for the part of Moira MacTaggert in its upcoming "X-Men" film. A majority of the "X-Men" cast, including Christopher Abbott as Professor X himself, was announced at Disney's D23 event in August. Since then, more castings have trickled out, such as Asa Germann ("Gen V") as Angel and Ben Wang ("The Long Walk") as Iceman.

Reinsve is known for her work with Norwegian filmmaker Joachim Trier, who directed her film debut (2011's "Oslo, 31 August"), her international breakout role (in 2021's "The Worst Person In The World"), and her first Best Actress Oscar nominated performance (for 2025's "Sentimental Value"). This past year, Reinsve starred in the creepypasta-inspired horror blockbuster "Backrooms" as Dr. Mary Kline, and she's one of the leads in the Norwegian social drama "Fjord." Incidentally, both of those teamed her up with leading men who've already joined the Marvel machine: Chiwetel Ejiofor and Sebastian Stan, respectively.

Now, Reinsve's casting as Moira is not confirmed yet. She's also previously said, on the "Happy Sad Confused" podcast, that "I don't have anything against [Marvel], and I respect that, but I don't think I could do it." But regardless of whether this casting goes through, this news suggests Marvel has a role planned for Moira MacTaggert in its "X-Men" films, which is news in and of itself.

Moira MacTaggert was co-created by Chris Claremont and Dave Cockrum, and she debuted near the very beginning of what would be Claremont's titanic 16-year run on the X-Men comics. She has consistently been one of Professor X's primary love interests alongside Shi'ar Queen Lilandra, as well as one of the X-Men's most important supporting characters.

In 1975's "X-Men" #96, Moira shows up at the X-Mansion's door and introduces herself as the X-Men's new housekeeper. In issues to come, she soon reveals she's much more. A genius geneticist with an expertise in mutants and a longtime ally of Professor Xavier, she maintains a "Mutant Research Center" on the fictional Muir Island (off the coast of her native Scotland).

One purpose of the Research Center is to contain dangerous mutants. Moira has a personal stake there, which comes to a head in an arc spanning "X-Men" #125-128 (by Claremont and John Byrne). Though Moira is seemingly a human herself, she's the mother of Proteus (Kevin MacTaggert), a malevolent mutant with reality-warping and body possession powers. (Kevin was conceived when Moira's then-husband Joseph MacTaggert raped her, and this original arc regressively suggests that Proteus is so evil because he's a child of rape.)

Moira has appeared in previous "X-Men" films. She briefly showed up in "X-Men: The Last Stand," played by Olivia Williams. Her research allows Xavier (Patrick Stewart) to resurrect himself by placing his consciousness inside his braindead twin brother. Moira played a bigger role in the prequel "X-Men" films. Portrayed by Rose Byrne in both "X-Men: First Class" and "X-Men: Apocalypse," this Moira was reimagined as an American CIA agent to fit the "James Bond" riffing of "First Class." But I say let the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Moira be Scottish, which was another touch to the internationalism of the "Second Genesis" X-Men team. (Wolverine is Canadian, Storm is African, Nightcrawler is German, Colossus is Russian, etc.)

Chris Claremont and Dave Cockrum's "X-Men" #104, when the X-Men first visit Muir Island, cheekily acknowledges the retcon that Professor X and Moira had been working together for many years. Cyclops tells Moira, "I've been with Professor Xavier from the beginning, and this is the first I've heard of your Mutant Research Center." Later writers would reveal Charles and Moira were hiding much deeper secrets than that.

Claremont ended Moira's journey in the 2000 crossover "Dream's End," when Moira perishes from her injuries after the Brotherhood of Mutants attack Muir Island. Unusually for a superhero comic character, she stayed dead for a long time — it took 19 years to reveal her death was faked, in Jonathan Hickman, Pepe Larraz, and R.B. Silva's interlocking miniseries "House of X/Powers of X."

This series revealed Moira is not only still alive but actually had been a mutant all along. Her power? Reincarnation. When she dies, the entire timeline resets around her, and she returns to the moment of her conception with all her memories. "House of X" #2 shows Moira has lived nine lives and, in most of them, she has tried and failed to find a solution to save mutantkind from annihilation by humanity and their robotic Sentinels. In her current life, her 10th, the solution is creating a mutant homeland: Krakoa.

While Jonathan Hickman consults on Marvel Studios scripts, it's not clear if the studio plans to adapt his "X-Men" stories. Moira's multiple lives, especially, might be tricky if Marvel wants to leave the multiverse storytelling behind after the boondoggle Multiverse Saga. But pulled off well, it could be as mind-blowing a twist as it was in the comics.

"X-Men" is set for a May 5, 2028 theatrical release.

#3527. You Can Get These 'Nothing' Over-Ear Headphones for $55 Right Now

Nothing, the upstart U.K. brand that makes products like phones, smartwatches, and headphones, has quickly become one of my favorite players in tech. Its products offer unique features and designs, and the prices are competitive. For example, right now, Nothing's latest budget over-ear headphones, which were released in October 2025, the CMF Headphone Pros, are just $55 (originally $99). This is a great option for anyone looking to get reasonably priced over-the-ear headphones that punch above their weight when it comes to performance.

Much like Nothing's CMF Buds Pro 2 earbuds, the CMF Headphone Pros are budget headphones that don't feel like it. They're an affordable alternative to the popular Headphone 1 (currently $199), and seamlessly integrate into the Nothing/CMF ecosystem, which includes smartphones, watches, and other audio products. There is a companion Nothing X app that allows you to customize action buttons, among other things, but the cool thing about these headphones is the control you get without needing the app.

There is a multi-function roller on one side of the headphone that you can roll to adjust volume or press to control the ANC modes, which include adaptive ANC (adjusting cancellation/transparency in real-time) and Spatial Audio (creates an immersive, 3D soundstage for music/movies). On the other side, you'll find an "Energy Slider," which tunes your sound in real-time, instantly adjusting the treble and bass balance.

You'll get an impressive 100 hours of playback on a single charge (reduced to up to 50 hours with ANC turned on) as well as AAC, SBC, and LDAC support. They have an IPX2 rating for resistance against sweat, and there is a 3.5mm audio jack for wired listening.

Nothing is known for its minimalistic design, but these headphones do a bit more by allowing you to mix and match the earcups with different colors (sold separately for $25). These are a good option for those looking for stylish, budget over-ear headphones that have great battery life and excellent audio quality for their price point.
